title: Add support for HTML rich text in Calendar Events in Calendar widget
line: Calendar event titles with formatting now show bold, italic and colored text in the Digital Clock's event list instead of raw HTML tags.
explanation: Some calendars (like the reporter's liturgical calendar .ics) store HTML formatting in the event summary. The Digital Clock agenda forced the title label to plain text, so the tags were printed literally, while the event description right below it already detects rich text. The change drops the plain-text override on the title so it auto-detects rich text like the description, and opens links in titles like the description does.

commits.message:
applets/digital-clock: show rich text in event titles

Event titles were always shown as plain text, so calendars that store
formatting in the summary showed raw HTML tags in the agenda. Let the
title detect rich text like the description below it already does.

BUG: 520844

media.caption: Events with HTML titles from the reporter's .ics show raw tags in the agenda
Same events with the fix: bold, colored and italic text; the plain title with < and & is unchanged

review.text: This is a minimal change that makes the title auto-detect rich text the same way the description right below it already does. The screenshots show the reporter's HTML summaries rendered properly while a plain title with < and & is unchanged. Strictly, an iCalendar SUMMARY is plain text, and KCalendarCore tracks summaryIsRich(); maintainers may prefer passing that flag through the event plugin API instead of guessing. Auto-detection also lets a calendar invite pull remote content into the title, but the description already allows the same, so this is consistent with existing behaviour.
